messages:
tim (customer): hi, we've been hitting weird failures on /v1/embeddings — sometimes we get a single-dim vector or a 400, other times a normal 1536-dim. started after a deploy. any idea?

jordan (support): sorry about that — can you paste the exact request body you send (raw JSON) and the error/response you see? also which client (fetch/axios/node) and model?

tim (customer): using a browser frontend with fetch -> our code does: const body = JSON.stringify({ model: 'embed-small', input: JSON.stringify(texts) }); fetch('/api/proxy', { method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body }); response has 400: "Invalid input shape" or sometimes returns an embedding array with a single element. repro curl I grabbed: 

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"embed-small","input":"[\"hello world\"]"}'

jordan (support): ah that looks like double-stringify. you're sending input as a string that contains JSON array text ("[\"hello world\"]") instead of an actual array. the API expects either a string (single item) or an array of strings. when we receive a JSON string that looks like an array, tokenization and downstream batching behave oddly and clients that assume a batch will get mismatched shapes.

maria (engineer): confirming — double-encoded input is the root cause here. examples:

Wrong (what you're sending):
{ "model": "embed-small", "input": "[\"a\"]" }  // input is a JSON string

Correct options:
1) single string: { "model": "embed-small", "input": "a" } -> returns one embedding vector
2) batch: { "model": "embed-small", "input": ["a", "b"] } -> returns list of embeddings

If the client sends the stringified array, the server treats that whole string as the single text to embed (including brackets), which leads to unexpected tokenization and sometimes a single embedding vector when you expected a batch. That explains the dimension/shape confusion.

jordan (support): quick repro steps I used locally:
1) curl with -d '{"model":"embed-small","input":"[\"x\"]"}' -> server returns a single embedding for the whole string (not a batch) or 400 depending on model precheck.
2) curl with -d '{"model":"embed-small","input":["x"]}' -> returns one embedding in a list as expected.

tim (customer): ohhh ok — we were doing JSON.stringify twice because we hand off to an internal proxy that also JSON.stringify's the body. thanks. two follow-ups: 1) after this happened we saw a billing spike (lots of tiny single requests), and 2) we got some 429s/latency. any recommendations for batching from the client side?

maria (engineer): for throughput/billing: avoid sending thousands of separate requests. Either send arrays of inputs in one request (batch up to the token limit) or throttle concurrency. Redwood runtime does some automatic batching but it's not a substitute for client-side grouping because of latency tradeoffs. Practical guidance:
- Group inputs into arrays of strings, e.g. batch_size = 16/32 depending on text length.
- Respect model token limit; don't batch across that.
- Use exponential backoff + jitter for 429s.
- If you're proxying, make sure the proxy forwards the JSON body as an object (not double-stringified).

Example client fix (JS):
// BAD: double-stringify
const body = JSON.stringify({ model: 'embed-small', input: JSON.stringify(texts) });
// GOOD: stringify once, pass array/object directly
const body = JSON.stringify({ model: 'embed-small', input: texts });

sam (ingest-bot): note added to ticket #INC-4821: "customer double-encoded embedding input causing shape mismatch and billing spike; recommended batching + proxy fix."

jordan (support): action items: tim to remove the extra JSON.stringify in proxy, add simple batching (client-side), and monitor for 429s. if you still see 400/shape mismatches, paste raw request body and response here and we'll escalate. :thumbsup:

tim (customer): will do, thanks all. saved me a ton of time. :relieved:
